sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Union County
sections.html:
Your town does. Union County is made up of 21 municipalities, and the county board's contact page lists a separate tax assessor and tax collector for each one, from Berkeley Heights and Clark to Westfield and Winfield. The county government does not send homeowners a bill. It runs the Union County Board of Taxation, which supervises assessment and hears appeals.

The Board of Taxation is at 300 North Avenue East in Westfield, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, at 908-527-4775 or uctaxboard@ucnj.org. For a seller the split is practical: ask your town's collector for a payoff statement, and ask your town's assessor about the value on the record.

Union County covers 105.41 square miles, with Elizabeth as its seat. The 2020 count was 137,298 people in Elizabeth alone, and the 2025 federal estimate for the county is 601,863. With 21 separate towns on a small footprint, a county-wide figure is only a starting point for pricing one house. About 43% of homes are rented.

With owner payments above $3,200 a month before any repairs, the property tax line is a major piece of what an owner carries. A successful appeal or a clean payoff at closing can change what a seller walks away with.

The cutoff is April 1 where the town has not revalued, May 1 where it has, or 45 days after the bulk mailing of the assessment notice. A cutoff that falls on a weekend or office holiday moves to the following business day.

  • Online filers have until 11:59:59 pm on the deadline date, and the system serves copies on the municipal clerk and assessor automatically.
  • Paper appeals must be physically in the Westfield office by 4:00 pm. A postmark does not count.
  • Added, omitted and rollback assessment appeals are due December 1 at 4:00 pm, or 30 days after the collector mails the tax bill.

One rule catches sellers who are behind: taxes and municipal charges must be paid through the first quarter of the current year, or the appeal can be dismissed for failure to pay.

The filing fee depends on the assessed value of the property, and it is non-refundable. Online filers pay a further $5 convenience charge. Paper filings need exact cash, a check or a money order payable to the Union County Tax Administrator.

Only an owner or an attorney may file. Real estate agents and appraisers cannot file or sign an appeal for an owner, because the state treats that as unauthorized practice of law. A corporation, partnership, LLC or trust must use an attorney unless the prior year's taxes were under $25,000.

sections.h2: The Chapter 123 ratio and your assessment
sections.html:
The ratio sets a value range around your town's average assessment ratio, and you win only if you prove the market value falls outside it. Each year the state studies sales in your municipality and publishes an average ratio plus a lower and an upper limit, spaced 15% below and above the average. Divide your total assessment by each ratio to get a market value range.

If your own estimate of the value on October 1 of the prior year falls inside that range, the board treats the assessment as correct. If you prove a value below the range, the board sets the new value by multiplying the market value by the average ratio. The ratios do not apply in a town that has just put a revaluation into effect, because the new assessment is then deemed market value and you only need to prove a figure below it.

sections.h2: Evidence that works at a hearing
sections.html:
The best evidence is recent arm's-length sales of comparable homes, supplied within the board's timeline. Sales must support the value as of October 1 of the year before the appeal. Sales outside the sampling window or between related parties can be disqualified. Sale records are available from your assessor, so confirm with that office that any sale you pick is counted as usable.

  • Evidence not filed with the petition must reach the board at least seven calendar days before the hearing, with copies to the assessor and municipal clerk.
  • Notices go out at least 10 days ahead, and hearings run from April through August, Tuesday through Friday.
  • Hearings run online, with a call-in option. Adjournments are rarely granted.

The board decides on the evidence submitted, so put your explanation of why the comparables fit your house in writing instead of saving it for a conversation.

Contact the collector in the town where the house sits and ask for a written payoff. Each of the 21 municipalities runs its own office with its own phone line, and the county board lists the collector contacts for each town. The assessor in the same town can tell you whether an added or omitted assessment is pending for new work on the house.

If you think the value is wrong, remember the filing windows are fixed and hearings run April through August. Ask the board about any petition already on file, and tell the buyer's side about it before closing. Gather your tax bills, your sale contract and any assessment notice, so the closing agent can settle the balance out of your proceeds.

A cash buyer purchasing as is can close without waiting for a hearing, but an unpaid balance still comes out of your proceeds, so get the payoff first.

faqs.q: Does Union County itself send my tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Each of the 21 municipalities bills its own taxes through its own tax collector. The county supervises assessment through the Board of Taxation in Westfield.

faqs.q: What is the Union County Board of Taxation phone number?
faqs.a: 908-527-4775. The office is at 300 North Avenue East, Westfield, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, and it can be reached by email at uctaxboard@ucnj.org.

faqs.q: Can my real estate agent file my tax appeal?
faqs.a: No. Only an owner or an attorney may file. Agents and appraisers cannot file or sign an appeal for a taxpayer.

faqs.q: Can I appeal if my property taxes are behind?
faqs.a: It can be dismissed. Taxes and municipal charges must be paid up through the first quarter of the current year when an appeal is filed.

faqs.q: When does a Union County tax appeal hearing take place?
faqs.a: Between April and August, Tuesday through Friday, online with a call-in option. Hearing notices are mailed at least 10 days before the date, and evidence is due seven calendar days beforehand.
